# New: Import a release's own files, such as its cue sheet and rip log

Part of the [custom Lidarr image](https://github.com/chodeus/Lidarr/tree/custom) (`ghcr.io/chodeus/lidarr:custom`), which merges this branch into `develop`. It is stacked on [`fix/extras-link-track-files`](https://github.com/chodeus/Lidarr/tree/fix/extras-link-track-files) and merges after it.

With Import Extra Files on, Lidarr imports only extra files named after a track, such as `01 - Song.lrc` beside `01 - Song.flac`. A release's own files, such as `Album.cue` or the rip log, never match a track's name, so they stay in the download folder.

- Once an album's tracks are imported, every file in their download folders that has a wanted extension and that no audio file's name starts goes into the folder the album's tracks share (their deepest common folder), under its own name and byte for byte. Every audio file in those folders counts, so the lyrics of a track that didn't import aren't taken for the release's. A folder gives release files only when each audio file in it other than an image came from this album's decisions, imported or not: a folder holding another album's tracks gives none, and neither does a single-file download, which sits in the client's shared folder.
- An audio file with a cue sheet of the same name beside it (regardless of case, as `Album.CUE` beside `Album.flac`) is an image, not a track, so its `.cue` and `.log` are the release's. After Unpackerr's `split_flac` splits an image, it sends Lidarr a manual import of the split tracks alone, and Lidarr imports them with the cue sheet and the rip log. On Lidarr's own import of that folder, the image matches no track and stays in the download. The row has the album and no track file: migration 915 lets `ExtraFiles.TrackFileId` be null, as `MetadataFiles` already allows.
- A release file is never written over an existing file: one an import that doesn't replace kept, one nothing recorded, or a second download folder's file of the same name. It is skipped with a warning. One whose row can't be saved is taken back out of the library (deleted if copied, moved back if moved), so it can't stand in the way of a later import.
- An import that replaces the album's files (every download import does; a manual import when asked to) first sends the previous release's files to the recycle bin, whatever the Import Extra Files setting, as the replaced tracks' own extras go whatever it says. One that can't be recycled keeps its row, so the next replacing import tries it again. One that doesn't replace keeps them, and so does one whose tracks come from inside the artist's folder, such as a client saving into the album's folder: the release files there are this release's own.
- Renaming moves a release file to the folder the album's tracks now share, keeping its name.
- Deleting the album with its files recycles its release files, with its other extras (from `fix/extras-link-track-files`). Removing its track files one at a time, a disk scan finding them gone, or removing the root folder leaves them on disk, until a replacing import or the album's deletion; housekeeping drops their rows once the album is gone.
- Wanted extensions match regardless of case and only after a dot: `log` matches `Album.LOG` but not `Album.backlog`. Before, `log` missed `.LOG` and matched `backlog`, for track-named files too.
- The Import Extra Files help text says so, and its examples now name lyrics, cue sheets and rip logs instead of subtitles and nfo. The Extra File Extensions setting's examples keep develop's text: another image branch adds a key on the next line, and the image's union merge of `en.json` would keep both versions of the line.

Tests, over the real services and test database: release files imported once into the album folder under their names (a UTF-16 cue sheet byte for byte, `.LOG` for `log`), with the track's lyrics still linked to the track; a track that didn't import keeps its lyrics out; a split image's cue sheet and rip log imported, whatever their case, and also when only the split tracks are imported, as Unpackerr's manual import sends them; no release files from a folder holding another album's audio or beside a single-file download; a replacing import recycles the previous release's files, also with Import Extra Files off, and one that doesn't replace keeps them; a release file that can't be recycled keeps its row; an import from inside the artist's folder keeps the album's release files; the import still published when the download client's path isn't valid here; nothing written over an existing file; a file whose row can't be saved taken back out; extension matching by case and after a dot; the migration keeping rows and storing one without a track file; a release file moved with its album's tracks across disc folders, another album's left alone; only the album's own release files recycled, kept when the album's last track file is removed, and recycled when the album is deleted with its files but not without; housekeeping keeping an album's release file and dropping one whose album is gone. Each was broken on purpose and caught by a test.

Full Core suite in Release: 3,334 pass. Merged after the custom build's 51 other branches and `fix/extras-link-track-files`, it merges cleanly and builds, `en.json` has no repeated keys, migration 915 is the only one with its number, and the Core suite there passes 4,687. In Debug, only the three tests that also fail without these branches fail: `should_remove_missing_import_lists_on_startup` and two `UpgradeMediaFileServiceFixture` tests for a file gone from disk.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **New Features**
  - A release's own files, such as its cue sheet and rip log, are imported once into the album's folder under their own names. A split image's cue sheet and rip log are the release's too, whatever their case, also when Unpackerr imports only the split tracks.
  - A replacing import first sends the previous release's files to the recycle bin, unless its tracks come from inside the artist's folder. One that can't be recycled keeps its row for the next replacing import.
  - Release files move with their album's tracks on rename, and are recycled when the album is deleted with its files. They stay when the album's last track file is removed.
- **Bug Fixes**
  - Extra file extensions match regardless of case and only after a dot.
  - A release file is never written over an existing file, and one whose row can't be saved is taken back out of the library. The release-file step can't stop an import's events, even when the download client's path isn't valid on this machine.
- **Documentation**
  - The Import Extra Files help text names lyrics, cue sheets and rip logs, and says a release's own files are imported once into the album's folder.
